decisions: Blocked on extract_modules.py until one line changes. Plan._residue_reads feeds every non-movable top-level statement to free_names, which wraps it in a function body; this source's 'from __future__ import annotations' makes symtable raise SyntaxError, so the CLI traces back instead of printing a plan. Fix: build kept from statements that are not MOVABLE and not ast.Import or ast.ImportFrom. An import binds names and never reads any, and _unread_imports already handles the import block separately, so nothing else moves. damage.py has no future import, which is why step 1 never hit this. Verified clean with that one change applied.

The cross-participant authority audit (map section I14) moves into ally_packet_shape.py, five defs past the roster's eleven. It is upstream of the packet, not downstream: _packet calls _check_cross_participant_authority, _check_declared_classes and _check_aura_arming on every packet it builds, and repriced_for_recipient calls producer_item, so leaving I14 in the residue is a back-edge from two modules. Auditing a packet against its declared authority is part of what a packet is, so the module docstring covers it. ally_packet_shape.py lands at 317 body lines and 8 internal imports, clear of both arms.

The five per-item-family branch modules the roster names (item_support_quests, item_support_everlasting, item_support_shred, item_support_enchanter, item_support_actives) are NOT in this assignment and cannot be. They are branches inside derive_item_support_effects, and extract_modules.py moves top-level units only. They need the hand carve the map describes first: each branch becomes a top-level _x_packets(ctx) -> list[dict] and derive_item_support_effects extends packets with each in the same order. Only then can they be named as defs here. Ledger insertion order is the float-sum trap, so the carve must preserve branch order exactly.

Consequence of stopping at three modules: the residue is 1550 lines and its size finding does not move, because derive_item_support_effects is 1256 of them. The three modules are still worth landing first: they are what the branch carve needs to import.

I4's cleanse builders (_support_quest_packets, _cleanse_active_packet, _cleanse_movement_entry, _self_cleanse_items) stay in the residue for now and travel with item_support_actives.py in the carve step, which is what holds support_event_view.py at 9 internal imports.

Landing this makes the CLAUDE.md quirk 'item_support_effects loads 15 internal modules ... only its reader count keeps that arm quiet' stale. Update it in the same commit as the carve, not before: the three modules alone do not lower the residue's import count enough to retire the note.
